basics.name: Viacheslav Deniskin
basics.label: PhD Candidate in Marketing (Consumer Behavior)
basics.summary: PhD Marketing Candidate at the University of Kansas with experience designing and analyzing 20+ experiments in Qualtrics and R, building reproducible data pipelines, and conducting large-scale topic modeling projects on brand activism and corporate social responsibility. Teaching experience includes redesigning and teaching an undergraduate Digital Marketing course focused on A/B testing and conversion optimization.

work.name: University of Kansas
work.summary: Graduate assistant in the Marketing area focusing on quantitative consumer research and undergraduate instruction in digital marketing.
highlights: Designed and analyzed 20+ experiments (N = 100–800 per study) in Qualtrics and R to quantify how messaging and brand positioning shape user attitudes, choice, and purchase behaviors.
Built reproducible R pipelines for data cleaning and statistical modeling to extract insights on behavioral patterns and estimate effect sizes.
Conducted a large-scale study of over 170 academic articles and used topic modeling to identify key insights into discrepancies between brand activism and corporate social responsibility.

Re-designed the syllabus and taught an undergraduate course on Digital Marketing for two semesters, focusing on A/B testing implementation and conversion optimization; achieved average student ratings of 4.2/5 and 4.6/5.
Guest-lectured on Influencer Marketing and Integrated Marketing Communications for over 100 students.

work.name: Kraft Heinz UK
work.summary: Summer internship in London supporting sales analytics and customer loyalty initiatives.
highlights: Designed and developed an interactive dashboard in Excel to visualize 600 rows of weekly data.
Improved efficiency of the field sales team by implementing 5 new KPIs through the dashboard.
Created reusable templates of loyalty schemes for the department to help attract more new customers and retain at least 30% more of the existing ones.
